analysis.title: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia does not mean back to normal for Asia
key_insights: Markets rallied on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, with Nvidia up 31% and the SOX up 14% in the rebound. The AI growth story script has changed though.
The eased risk is the leadership vacuum at Nvidia. Investors had feared a successor would rethink the product roadmap, supplier orders and AI build-out financing.
Taiwan activated its stabilization fund and curbed short selling during the drag, and South Korea prepared similar support.
Huang's return comes with a new board committee on national security and export controls and a chief compliance officer to be hired. His open-weight AI and China stances will face challenges.
New US chip rules on remote access mainly affect Southeast Asia. Investors should not assume restrictions have peaked.
The backlash is bipartisan. Huang testifies before the Senate Banking Committee on 3 December and privately before the House on 1 December, and Democrats take control of Congress in January 2027.

Proposed legislation includes the MATCH Act (immersion DUV ban to China), AI Overwatch Act (congressional veto on China chip licenses), Chip Security Act (location reporting) and Remote Access Security Act (passed House 12 January 2026, pending in Senate).
For Asia, the risk of a leaderless Nvidia is gone, which should ease pressure on export demand and sentiment. US-China rivalry and security outranking commerce remain unchanged.

market_movers.rationale: Shares rebounded 31% on Huang's return, but new compliance governance and bipartisan political scrutiny limit a return to normal.

sector_views.rationale: Leadership risk has eased but export control and legislative risks are rising, so the old normal has not returned.

risk_factors: Further US export restrictions, including legislation from a Democrat-controlled Congress from January 2027.
Senate and House hearings on Nvidia on 1 and 3 December could bring further investigations.
Challenges to Huang's open-weight AI and China stances.
Remote access rules hitting Southeast Asian data centres and Chinese cloud customers.
vol_and_positioning: Taiwan curbed short selling and activated its stabilization fund during the Nvidia-related selloff.
geopolitical: US-China tech rivalry continues, with security outranking commerce whatever Trump agrees with Xi.
New US remote access rule effective 19 November 2026 requires licenses for covered chip exports to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, with a 90-day transition for existing services.
Blackwell exports to China face a presumption of denial and H200 requires case-by-case US approval.
Proposed MATCH Act would ban immersion DUV sales to China and push allies to align, affecting Japanese equipment suppliers.
Taiwan and South Korea moved to stabilize markets during the Nvidia leadership turmoil.

tension_points.bull_case: Huang's return removes the leadership vacuum risk, easing fears over roadmap, supplier orders and AI financing, and supports export demand and sentiment.
tension_points.bear_case: Nothing returns to normal, with a new national security committee, bipartisan backlash, hearings and further potential chip restrictions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Escalation at the 3 December Senate Banking Committee hearing or passage of restrictive legislation such as the MATCH Act or Remote Access Security Act.
